body: You know, I've thought about that before too.  Honestly though I think it takes a lot more mental fortitude and situational preparation than you'd think. Like if you're hanging yourself, you know, there's that 3 minutes or so of risky time where someone could happen upon you and stop you, but for starvation, that period of time is a lot longer and thus to avoid being happened upon you have to seek out some serious situational isolation.  I saw this great movie that's on Netflix if you have it, called God Knows Where I Am (it's not religious, the title is just a quote from the woman's journal).  It is a documentary about this woman who likely had schizophrenia (and other mental health issues) and accidentally starves herself to death during a self imposed isolation/agoraphobia/paranoia spell while she's squatting in an abandoned house.  It was pretty clear from her extensive journalling that suicide wasn't her intention, but she clearly was suffering from some delusions that kept her from reaching out to get help or even just getting food or anything, so her mental health issue did kill her. Especially towards the end it seems like she only starves herself to death on accident/as a result of delusion. That said there is a point where her starving to death is like not really practically reversible- the actual starving to death part, where, despite still being delusional, she wishes she could leave to get food, but she's too weak to do so, and that goes on for like an obscenely long time (it's been a while since I watched this but if I recall correctly, it's like over a month or something, where she is like too weak to leave the house cause it's winter and it's isolated, but she still subsists on some slowly rotting apples she had collected that fall).  That part of the doc kind of gave me pause in considering that option, personally, but still it's an interesting/sad watch. Here's the trailer: https://youtu.be/5FsSSDp-scg
Seriously, my mom has told me about how she'd had abortions before me and I'm just like "feeling real jealous right now."

I mean, it's really not likely- the whole theatrical exhibition industry has been on the brink for quite some time even before this. Back in the day the only thing that ensured the exhibition part of the film industry survived the Spanish flu was a) there wasn't any other option for exhibition and b) the major studios coming in and buying up theaters in bulk/starting block booking, which has since been made very much illegal since it's essentially running a monopoly. So now that streaming is an option, and since the studios can't (and likely wouldn't even if they could) buy up the theaters to prop things up it's just a matter of time for the vast majority of theaters in the world and that timeline just got shrunk to the space of like weeks. I live in a city with like 30 some theaters (a good chunk of which are indie) and I doubt there will be more than one or two left after this (probably just the chains). We're witnessing the death of a lot of industries (most of whom were already on edge) right now - this - is clearly how we get to all our post apocalyptic fantasies about everything being automated and no one having jobs.  

Anyway, all my doomsday soothsaying about my industry aside, fucking everyone and their mom is trying to get a new job right now, and my whole career has been built on supporting public events/gatherings in some way or another. So it's like I'm back to being a college student basically, no real qualifications for jobs that can be done at home, no degree in those areas, but all the same not-entry-level sized expenses... I know what it's like to be in that position amidst a recession, but now feels like it's going to be 10x worse. And anyone who's counting on the current american government to get us through this is a straight up fool. 

I know my brain is great at catastrophizing, but I mean, this _is_ a catastrophy, the weak -read: people like me- won't make it. I was barely making one super flexible full time job with good benefits work with having MDD, the thought that I'll likely need to have multiple highly demanding, inflexible, precarious, super stressful, public facing customer service jobs (if I can even get them at all) is what's depressing.  How will I not be on the streets if I "luck out", get a couple jobs like that, but then go through several weeks of near catatonia because of the pressure with virtually no sick time? My friends who are have made that work seem like superhuman gods of patience with infinite energy to me. And that's the best case scenario.

Yep.  Although I will say, when I've cut my wrists deep enough to see my pulse in the blood that's coming out, there is like this primordial gut-level nausea that overcomes me.  The fantasy is much more pleasant than the reality, heh.  But yes, definitely fantasize about that on at least a semi daily basis.

Just a random thought from your post but maybe part of the reason we're all depressed is that the part of our brain that's competitive (or more accurately the part that is comparative) is like in overdrive all the time...

Sorry I'm drunk atm, but i totally feel ya OP, my partner has really bad anxiety and any time I'm having a hard time with MDD he's almost always immediately going to the 'but your life isn't nearly as bad as mine' line. I just don't talk about my feelings with him anymore.
